1: The patient presents with a painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region, which is consistent with a hernia. The ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass tracking into the inguinal canal support this diagnosis. The absence of symptoms such as pain, changes in appetite or bowel habits, urinary symptoms, weight loss, infection, or bleeding also points towards a benign condition like a hernia.
